svg.title: Runtime governance
svg.desc: An inbound channel message passes the pause intercept, admin commands, thread-binding lookup and per-sender limit, then the MessageQueue. Every turn on any surface then passes ExecutionCoordinator.acquire: the daily token budget, the session lock, loop pre-checks and the global rate window, and only then is an execution lane chosen. Tool-fingerprint detection and turn limits run while the provider turn executes.

g.text: Hover a step for what it enforces; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: Every turn on every surface passes one admission point before a provider process can start.

g.text: INBOUND CHANNEL MESSAGE · before any turn exists · channel-level limits live here
ADMISSION · ExecutionCoordinator.acquire · admitTurn, then the lane · EVERY SURFACE
pause intercept · while PauseController is paused, every non-reserved channel message is queued and acknowledged
Web chat, tasks and scheduled jobs are not paused. In-memory, resets on restart; max_pause_queued caps one non-admin sender.
admin commands · ReservedCommandHandler runs before rate limiting so emergency commands work during a flood
A non-admin sender gets "Only admin senders can use this command." and an audit entry (guard ReservedCommand, hook channel_command).
thread binding · tryHandle order: reserved command, thread-binding lookup, per-sender rate limit, bound-thread routing
Only task bindings route; run bindings (workflow.chat_notifications) route nothing, so a bound thread is rate-limited like any other.
sender limit · governance.rate_limits.per_sender.messages per window; SlidingWindowRateLimiter, in-memory, lazy eviction
An empty admin_senders list makes everyone an admin, so the limit never fires; review requests are ordinary turns and are limited.
MessageQueue · per-session queue with a global concurrency cap; max_queue_depth and max_queued reject with a queue-full reply
max_queued is skipped for admins. A budget-exhausted turn gets a polite reply and no retry.
token budget · reads the day total from UsageTracker (usage_daily:YYYY-MM-DD); one warning per day, shared by both thresholds
Read-only check; BudgetExhaustedException fails a task non-retryably (budgetExceeded). A storage failure surfaces, never silently allows.
session lock · taken before the state-recording checks, so an attempt the global cap rejects is not counted
Polled fail-fast requests (tasks, workflow steps) take the worker permit before admission for the same reason.
loop pre-checks · a human message resets the chain depth; each mechanism is disabled by a 0 threshold
LoopDetectedException fails a task as loopDetected; the detector returns results and TurnGovernanceEnforcer decides the action.
turn rate window · governance.rate_limits.global.turns per window (default 0 = off); SSE rate_limit_warning at 80%, re-armed below 60%
Records state, so it runs after the lock. The deployment-wide limiter is built once and shared by every runner.
execution lane · the coordinator alone chooses the fixed primary lane or a provider worker lease, after governance admission
providers.<id>.pool_size is the later hard execution bound, not a substitute for governance.
at the threshold, abort cancels the turn
tool fingerprint · consecutive identical tool calls (name plus key-sorted canonical JSON arguments) within one turn
Under abort the running turn is cancelled (reason automationCancel) and [Loop detected: ...] is recorded as the assistant message.
turn limits · governance.turn_limits bounds one provider turn; the only governance controls that are on by default
A breach cancels through the same path as a user cancel. 0 disables either limit.
at this point it only warns
after the turn · the tokens are already spent, so the next admitTurn pre-check is what aborts if the window is still over
Per-turn fingerprint state is cleaned in the turn's finally.
